panels.visual: The completed Parthenon in bright painted colours (blue, red and gold pediments) glowing on the Acropolis, crowds of Athenians below, Glauka the owl in the sky
panels.caption: The Parthenon, built between 447 and 432 BC, when Pericles led Athens.

panels.visual: Phidias (balding sculptor, strong forearms, chisel) and the architects Ictinus and Callicrates bent over plans of the temple on a table, Pericles looking over their shoulders
panels.caption: He chose the best: the sculptor Phidias and two architects, Ictinus and Callicrates.

panels.visual: Interior view: a gigantic twelve-metre statue of Athena in gold and ivory, helmet and spear, towering over tiny worshippers; ray of light
panels.caption: Inside stood Athena, twelve metres tall, gold and ivory.

panels.visual: A sculptor with a chisel and a hammer (Phidias, balding, strong forearms) proudly stepping back from the statue's foot
panels.caption: Made by the sculptor Phidias.

panels.visual: Dramatic diagram-like drawing of the Parthenon with exaggerated curves: the floor bulging up in the middle, columns swelling and leaning inward, thin red guide lines, Glauka pointing with a wing
panels.caption: Almost no straight lines in the whole building.

speech.speaker: Glauka
speech.text: The floor rises in the middle!

panels.visual: Close-up of a column swelling in the middle, tape measure and an amazed builder
panels.caption: The columns swell and lean slightly inward.

panels.visual: The Parthenon from far away looking perfectly straight, a tiny girl-shaped visitor in the foreground squinting
panels.caption: From a distance it looks perfectly straight.

panels.visual: The Parthenon painted in vivid colours (blue, red, gold) compared with a ghostly white modern version drawn in thin outline on the side
panels.caption: It was painted in bright colours, not the white we see now.

panels.visual: A crowd of angry Athenian officials in the Agora pointing at Phidias, who stands calm, arms folded, a scroll of accusation on the floor
panels.caption: Phidias was accused of stealing the gold.

panels.visual: Phidias cleverly unlocking the gold robe plates from the statue of Athena, plates lying in a neat pile
panels.caption: He had built the statue so the gold could be lifted off and weighed.

panels.visual: A huge pair of scales with the gold plates on one side and a weight on the other, officials leaning in with eyes popping out of their heads
panels.caption: They weighed it.

panels.visual: Phidias grinning smugly with arms folded; the scale perfectly balanced; officials with embarrassed sweat drops
panels.caption: It was all there.
